sentences.text: In a mouse model simulating brain hemorrhage, researchers tracked the spread and removal of red blood cells following the bleed.
These cells traveled along cranial nerves into the lymphatic system, while many became trapped in collagen-lined spaces adjacent to large veins in the brain's lining.
By the second day after the injury, immune cells known as macrophages removed some of these trapped red blood cells.
The authors suggest that these specific structures and cells could be targeted to help the brain recover faster from a stroke.
